content:
maria: Heads-up — we need a new mixed GPU nodepool in us-west4 for the low-latency gen workload.
maria: Goal: <100ms tail for the realtime endpoint. Secondary: cheap batch throughput for offline jobs.
maria: Proposal: two pools — reserved A100 nodes (latency SLA) + preemptible A10G nodes (batch). CA handles scale.
josh: +1 to split pools. We should taint the A100 pool so only latency pods land there unless they tolerate taint.
josh: Also need separate autoscaler configs: fast scale-up and no aggressive scale-down for A100; slower for A10G.
leo: Question: do we have the quota to spin up A100s in us-west4? Last I checked quota for a100-gpu was low in that region.
cloud-ops-bot: Current GPU quota in us-west4: A100 = 8 GPUs used / 16 quota. A10G = 24 GPUs used / 48 quota. vCPU quota remaining low in us-west4: 120 vCPU free.
tanya: If A100 quota is tight, we could use a 1:5 pod placement — small reserved pool with high-availability AZ spread, and scale-burst to A10G with on-demand fallback.
tanya: Implementation notes: taint A100 nodes: "realtime=true:NoSchedule" and add toleration only to the realtime Deployment.
rishi: Be careful with PodDisruptionBudgets — if PDBs prevent scale-down we might lose cost savings. For A10G batch, keep min replicas 0 and no PDB.
maria: Good call. For autoscaler flags I was thinking: --scale-down-delay=10m for A100 pool, --max-node-provision-time=5m for fast scale-up, and CA scale-up-concurrency tuned.
josh: Also enable binpacking (prefer packing into A10G) for cheaper per-node efficiency, but ensure the scheduler doesn't evict latency pods.
leo: On cloud quota: I'll open a quota request ticket for A100 to bump to 32 GPUs in us-west4. Ticket: CLOUD-REQ-5872. ETA 48-72h.
leo: Patch to nodepool spec (preview):
```yaml
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: infer-a100-reserved
spec:
  machineType: n1-standard-16
  accelerators:
    - type: nvidia-a100
      count: 1
  taints:
    - key: "realtime"
      value: "true"
      effect: "NO_SCHEDULE"
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 1
    maxNodeCount: 8
``` 
maria: That looks good. For the A10G pool we should set preemptible and aggressive autoscale min 0 max 30.
rishi: Watch kubelet logs on mixed pools — we saw device-plugin flapping last month after driver upgrades. Ensure GPU node image has matching NVIDIA driver + plugin version.
maria: Good reminder. We'll pin the GPU driver and run the device-plugin helm chart version >= 0.13.0.
josh: Ops checklist before provisioning:
- confirm quota bump (leo)
- update CA config and per-pool flags (maria/rishi)
- create nodepool manifests and taints/tolerations (maria)
- run canary with 5 latency pods to monitor tail latency (tanya)
maria: I'll start creating the manifests and open a PR. Can someone pair on the canary run tomorrow morning? :eyes:
tanya: I can run the canary at 09:00 PT. Will capture p50/p95/p99 from the tracing dashboard.
cloud-ops-bot: Note: currently 2 zones in us-west4 are experiencing minor provisioning delays — expect 5-10% slower startup times for new VMs.
josh: If provisioning delay persists we should increase max-node-provision-time in CA to avoid premature scale-down/backoff loops.
maria: Thanks all — filing the infra task and linking the PR when ready. I'll tag @cloud-ops and @rishi for review. :thumbsup:
